clue.text: Gold bangle — asset converted where labourer cleaned up

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gold bracelet is cashed in at the place where some worker once did a cleaning job.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'labourer' is Hercules, whose fifth labour was cleaning King Augeas's filthy stables in a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules cleaned the stables of King Augeas as one of his twelve labours, diverting rivers through them.

clue.text: Characters from Rye thus observed in Argyle?

definitions.text: Characters from Rye thus observed in Argyle?

parts.words: Characters from Rye thus observed in Argyle?
parts.note: taking every other letter of Argyle gives R, Y and E, so the letters of Rye are seen in Argyle in this way

explanation.surface: Visitors from the Sussex town of Rye are spotted in the Scottish county of Argyll.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye looks like a town and Argyle like a place or a sock pattern; really they are just strings of letters, and the second, fourth and sixth letters of ARGYLE spell RYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Picking every second letter is taking them in turn, one on and one off, which is the sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Instrument one exported from African country

indicators.note: exported means sent out of the country, so the letter is taken out of the country's name

parts.note: Gambia is a West African country
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is sent abroad from somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamba is the short name for the viola da gamba, a bowed string instrument held between the legs, and also an organ stop.

clue.text: Alsatians let loose to find aggressor

indicators.note: dogs let loose run wild, so the letters of the dog breed are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Guard dogs are released to track down an attacker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a person who attacks another; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: European ensnared in small deception

indicators.note: something ensnared is caught inside a trap, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: slight means small or minor

explanation.surface: A European is caught up in a minor piece of trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight, as in sleight of hand, is cunning trickery used to deceive.

clue.text: Improvised excellent book about Donegal's borders

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the first pieces go around the letters taken from the county

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the figure 1 written as the letter I

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something made up on the spot is a fine book about the edges of an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: Donegal is a county in the north-west of Ireland. A1 is a common way of saying excellent, and its 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to speak or perform without preparation, so the hyphenated adjective describes something made up as one goes.

clue.text: Liberal revelling in danger in Soviet city

indicators.note: revelling suggests wild, riotous behaviour, so the letters of the following words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A politician of the Liberal party enjoys himself despite being in peril.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Soviet-era name of St Petersburg, used from 1924 until 1991.

clue.text: MI6 finds relative shortly

indicators.note: shortly means in brief, so the word is cut short by losing its end

parts.note: a sister is a family relative

explanation.surface: The British spy agency tracks down a family member in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: MI6 is Britain's foreign intelligence agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Secret Intelligence Service is the official name of the British agency popularly called MI6, and these are its initials.

clue.text: Support second article having expunged first

indicators.note: expunged means wiped out, so the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an item is an article, as in a newspaper or a list

explanation.surface: A supporting piece of writing has had its opening part deleted.
explanation.definitionFit: A stem is the stalk that holds up a flower or leaf, or the slender upright part supporting a glass bowl.

clue.text: Consider some text in manuscript for propriety

parts.note: to see a matter is to consider it

indicators.note: in places the text inside the abbreviation

parts.note: a few lines are some text

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to weigh up a passage in an old document for correct behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe conduct that is fitting and in keeping with accepted standards of decorum.

clue.text: Paying for others to dine in Hertfordshire town?

indicators.note: in places the eating word inside the town's name

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Picking up the bill so friends can have dinner in a small English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hertfordshire is a county just north of London; Tring is one of its small towns.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone is to pay for their meal or drink as a gift.

clue.text: Drive out in attempt to cross North Island

indicators.note: to cross here is to go across, so the attempt word spans the two letters

parts.note: a bash is an informal word for an attempt, as in have a bash

explanation.surface: A motorist has a go at driving across the North Island of New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone from a place is to force them away, as an exile is sent abroad.

clue.text: Bloody genius on USA reforms

indicators.note: reforms means shapes again, so the letters are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: A brilliant person's ideas about changing America are described with a British expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means relating to blood or bloodshed, a literal sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Drunken priests initially botching psalm in services

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of the word is taken
in places the sung piece inside the tennis word

parts.note: in tennis, aces are unreturnable services
a chant is a sung psalm or prayer

explanation.surface: Tipsy clergy make a mess of a hymn during church services.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the frenzied priestesses and followers of Bacchus, the Roman god of wine, famous for drunken rites.

clue.text: French count runs round for Holy Spirit?

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the title and letter go around the word for

parts.note: comte is the French title for a count
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A French nobleman goes running in search of a divine presence.
explanation.definitionFit: In John's Gospel Jesus calls the Holy Spirit the Comforter, the one who consoles believers; the question mark flags this name.

clue.text: Singular fruit with perfect flavour

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a pear is a fruit
mint means perfect, as in mint condition

explanation.surface: A single fruit in flawless condition has a fine taste.
explanation.definitionFit: This mint is used to flavour gum, sweets and toothpaste, so the name is used of the taste itself.

clue.text: Coiffeur in Keighley shows where curlers are found

indicators.note: shows means displays, so the word is visible inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: A hairdresser in a Yorkshire town reveals where hair curlers are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: The hairdresser makes 'curlers' look like hair rollers, but they are players of curling, the sport of sliding stones over ice. Keighley is a town in West Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Curling is played on a sheet of ice called by this name, as for skating or ice hockey.

clue.text: Eleven minutes after the interval at Lord's

indicators.note: after places the minutes letter behind the break

parts.note: in a cricket match the afternoon break is tea; Lord's is the famous London cricket ground

explanation.surface: A cricket side comes out eleven minutes after the break at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eleven minutes' reads as a time span, but Eleven is the definition: a cricket side has eleven players. Lord's is a London cricket ground where play stops for tea in the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has eleven players, so an eleven is a playing side.

clue.text: Our set raving about repair that's fantastic

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters surround the repair word
raving means wild or mad, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: to mend is to repair

explanation.surface: Our group gets excited about a marvellous repair job.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words of praise meaning extremely good or impressive.

clue.text: Sound final whistle, perhaps, leading to drama

definitions.meaning: blowing the last whistle in a match brings a match to a close, read as two words
a play by Samuel Beckett, first staged in 1957

explanation.surface: A referee blows to finish the match, which leads to some theatrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means finish the match; as one it is the title of a Beckett play and the last phase of a chess game.

clue.text: Superman repelled by feeding dog that lacks tail

indicators.note: feeding means going into a mouth, so the turned word goes inside the dog
the tail of a word is its last letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a corgi is a breed of dog

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the word by is turned around

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero is driven back by a dog with no tail as he feeds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A being part human and part machine, with powers beyond ordinary people, is a kind of superhuman.

clue.text: Bird black in colour? Not completely!

indicators.note: in places the letter for black inside the shortened colour
not completely means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: green is a colour
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A bird is black, or at least partly so.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a diving water bird, such as the great crested one found on lakes.

clue.text: Stepped over mud outside new Ruhr location

indicators.note: over means turned back to front, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: trod means stepped

indicators.note: outside means around, so the mud word surrounds the letter for new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone steps over muddy ground outside a new site in industrial Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large city in the Ruhr, the industrial region of western Germany.

clue.text: Chop's rotten at one end, consumed by rodents

indicators.note: consumed by means eaten, so the letter goes inside the rodents

parts.note: mice are rodents

indicators.note: one end of the word here means its final letter

explanation.surface: A cut of meat has gone bad at one end and been eaten by vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop's' is read as 'Chop is', so the definition is the verb chop.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut food into very small pieces is to chop it finely, as with onions or meat.

clue.text: Celebs refuse to enter Georgia — and it's over

indicators.note: to enter means to go in, so the rubbish word goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia
litter is refuse or rubbish

indicators.note: over means turned round, so the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: Famous people throw rubbish into a US state and declare things finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like a verb (decline) but is the noun rubbish; 'over' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a collective word for fashionable, famous people, a play on literati.

clue.text: Note adviser initially grasped in left hand

indicators.note: grasped in a hand means held within it, so the letter goes between the other two
initially means at the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A written note from a counsellor is held in someone's left hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa this is the sixth note of the scale, also spelt la.

clue.text: Approval withheld in retreat?

parts.note: read as two words it says no to approval, a refusal of the okay; as one it is a secluded corner

explanation.surface: Permission is refused while an army falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' suggests an army falling back, but it is a hideaway; split the answer two letters in and it reads as 'no' plus 'okay'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sheltered corner or recess is a quiet hideaway where one can withdraw from others.

clue.text: Arab perhaps down for an old movie

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: An Arabian steed is brought down for a classic film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a direction but is the soft plumage of birds. The film is a 1932 Marx Brothers comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1932 Marx Brothers comedy film, also a slang word for nonsense.
